text: Backpack lists 1,200+ stocks and ETFs in its brokerage. Its catalog of Backpack-issued Solana tokens has 91. That's the gap in @solana's wallet vision: brokerage access covers far more shares than wallet withdrawal today.

sources.claim: Solana's November 7 clip quotes Backpack CEO Armani Ferrante describing a future where global brokerage assets are accessible from a self-custodial wallet.
Backpack advertises 1,200+ brokerage stocks and ETFs; only eligible stocks may be withdrawn to Solana, and stock services are limited to eligible jurisdictions.
Backpack's tokenized-securities catalog lists 91 Backpack-issued Solana assets (80 stocks and 11 ETFs/funds).

source_reply: Backpack's catalogs, checked 9 Nov: 1,200+ brokerage listings https://backpack.exchange/about/stocks and 91 Backpack-issued Solana tokens https://ui.backpack.exchange/tokenized-stocks/assets. These are different catalogs, not a count of every stock token on Solana. Stock access also depends on jurisdiction.
note: Contribution beyond the quoted vision: compares Backpack's present brokerage catalog with its own issued Solana-token catalog. The 1,200+ versus 91 gap establishes that brokerage availability and wallet withdrawal are currently different scopes. Primary Backpack catalog pages support both counts; the source reply states the scope and jurisdiction limit. No allegation about backing or redemption is made. Yesterday's post concerned LP PnL, so this is a different argument.
